title: That One Should Avoid Being Despised and Hated
coreMove: Prevent conspiracy by avoiding the paired failures that invite it: hatred from injury and contempt from weakness.
sourcePressure: The chapter gathers the earlier conduct lessons under two fatal reputational failures. Rapacity and violations of property and honor create hatred; fickleness, frivolity, weakness, and irresolution create contempt. Popular esteem makes conspiracy dangerous to conspirators, institutions can absorb reproach, and Roman emperors show the difficulty of satisfying people, nobles, and soldiers without becoming hated or despised.
chapterSpecificMisunderstanding: The wrong version becomes reputation management or likability advice. The writer must show the conspiracy logic: a plotter needs malcontents and expects popular approval, so a prince who is esteemed and not hated makes conspiracy harder before it starts.

counterintuition: most people think reputation is image, but actually it is survival
haters are dangerous, so avoid all criticism
tryThisNow: set a timer for ninety seconds and list who dislikes you

exampleSpecs.domain: a capital magistrate tempted to seize townhouse dowries after a treasury shortfall
exampleSpecs.audience: a prince deciding whether revenue need justifies touching property and honor together
exampleSpecs.stakes: the seizure funds soldiers for a month but gives every household a private reason to bless the assassin
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: The prince lifts the dowry keys from the seizure basket, returns them to the family seals, and orders the treasury search to stop at public contracts.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: Dowry keys lie in a seizure basket beside family seals.

exampleSpecs.domain: a court where petitioners reverse their stories because the ruler changes judgments every market day
exampleSpecs.audience: a ruler whose fickle decisions make every subject think he can be worked around
exampleSpecs.stakes: contempt grows when judgments look purchasable or reversible, making deception seem easy and conspiracy less frightening
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Before the next petition, the judge nails yesterday's judgment tablet beside today's docket and refuses to reopen it after the silk purse appears.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: Yesterday's judgment tablet hangs beside a silk purse on the docket rail.

exampleSpecs.domain: a Bologna-style city after conspirators kill a popular householder-prince but misread the crowd
exampleSpecs.audience: a chronicler showing why popular goodwill changes the conspirator's calculation
exampleSpecs.stakes: the assassins expect welcome, but the people see removal as an offense against themselves
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: The conspirators open the palace shutter expecting cheers, then see shopkeepers overturn the market tables into barricades against them.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: A palace shutter opens above market tables beginning to overturn.

exampleSpecs.domain: a kingdom using an independent high court to punish nobles without making every sentence the king's personal reproach
exampleSpecs.audience: a ruler balancing noble ambition and popular fear of noble violence
exampleSpecs.stakes: if the king personally beats down every noble, he earns their hatred; if he neglects the people, he loses their satisfaction
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: The king keeps the pardon ribbons on his own table while the high court bell rings for the noble sentencing across the square.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: Pardon ribbons sit on a royal table while a high court bell rope hangs across the square.

exampleSpecs.domain: an imperial camp where soldiers love rapacity but the capital wants peace
exampleSpecs.audience: a new emperor deciding which hatred he can least afford without being despised by the army
exampleSpecs.stakes: satisfying soldiers by plunder may make the people hate him, but appearing weak before veterans invites contempt and murder
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: He places the veterans' double-pay tablet beside the capital grievance roll and marks which group can destroy him first if left wholly hostile.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: A double-pay tablet lies beside a capital grievance roll.

exampleSpecs.domain: a provincial ruler keeping a threatened bodyguard officer after insulting his dead brother
exampleSpecs.audience: a security council learning why some personal injuries cannot be managed by general popularity
exampleSpecs.stakes: most plots are rare and difficult, but a desperate injured guard with daily access changes the danger calculus
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: The council finds the officer's access token still on the nightstand beside the unanswered petition about his brother's dishonor.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: A bodyguard access token lies beside an unanswered brother-honor petition.

skillTargets: distinguish actions that generate hatred from those that generate contempt
analyze why popular goodwill makes conspiracy dangerous for conspirators
apply the role of institutions in carrying reproach while the prince keeps grace
evaluate difficult cases where people, nobles, or soldiers have conflicting humors and different power to harm

tryThisNowSpec: Choose one ruler who faced a conspiracy. Mark the injuries that could create hatred, the signs that could create contempt, and whether the conspirators could expect the people to welcome the removal.
